correctness.rationale: PASS. For a finite connected triangle-free graph all of whose four-cycles are edge-disjoint, a nonadjacent pair has at most two common neighbors; two identify a unique square opposite pair. Neighbor subsets of size ≥2 other than those square diagonals therefore have unique closed-neighborhood centers. Decreasing-cardinality free-face pairing (sigma, sigma∪{center}) removes all and only their associated cells, leaving the original graph together with a tetrahedral boundary for each square. Edge-disjointness and triangle-freeness force distinct squares to share at most one vertex, so each square has separate interior diagonals; one of its two disk triangulations can be collapsed across its private rim edge while the other adds a null-attached S². Removing q distinct rim edges leaves a connected graph rank e−v+1−q; their cycle classes form a primitive direct summand (evaluating on the q rim edges). The oriented tetrahedral boundaries provide the claimed signed integral automorphism permutation module and H1 quotient; no equivariant wedge is inferred. Inspected verify.py exhaustively checks connected labeled graphs n=3..6 (3195; 1323 with squares), explicit collapsing and mod-two homology, plus randomized and noncactus examples. The q=0 square-free special case is acknowledged prior. The finite checks corroborate, not prove, the universal argument.
